item.text: The reconnaissance now establishes the key attribution frame: Biden was the federal executive decision-maker for national policy, diplomacy, appointments, and agency direction, while Congress, courts, states, local police, the Federal Reserve, and allied governments imposed material constraints. I’m carrying that distinction into the chapter ledger, especially for domestic policing, monetary policy, and Ukraine conduct.

Research pass completed for Joe Biden, United States, 2022. No scores or score ranges assigned.

Writes were unavailable because the workspace is read-only, so the complete ledger handoff is included here rather than persisted to the requested paths.

### Authority and evidence environment

- The President held formal responsibility for federal law execution, agency and Cabinet appointments, diplomacy, executive orders, and federal judges. Congress retained legislative, budgetary, treaty, confirmation, war, and oversight powers. [White House executive-branch description](https://www.whitehouse.gov/government/executive-branch/), [White House legislative-branch description](https://www.whitehouse.gov/government/legislative-branch/).
- Evidence visibility was high: official records, CRS/GAO audits, congressional investigations, courts, NGOs, and extensive media coverage were available. This creates open-society reporting-volume bias but also strong scrutiny and correction channels.
- State/local policing, Federal Reserve outcomes, congressional legislation, courts, and allied conduct were not automatically attributed to Biden.

### Global evidence ledger

Stable provisional IDs drafted: EV001–EV026.

Key evidence included:

- EV001–EV002: formal presidential authority and congressional constraints.
- EV003–EV005: Biden’s New START extension, Strategic Stability Dialogue, 2022 Nuclear Posture Review, arms-control and risk-reduction posture. [CRS arms-control report](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/RL/HTML/RL33865.html)
- EV006–EV008: Ukraine security assistance, congressional appropriations, and creation of end-use/accountability oversight mechanisms. [CRS Ukraine report](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/HTML/R47068.web.html)
- EV007: UN documentation of civilian harm, humanitarian access concerns, investigation, and ceasefire calls in Ukraine. [UN Ukraine statement](https://ukraine.un.org/en/176730-statement-un-resident-humanitarian-coordinator-osnat-lubrani-behalf-united-nations-ukraine)
- EV009–EV010: DOJ voting-rights enforcement and the December 2022 January 6 Committee report release. [DOJ voting-rights actions](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-releases-information-efforts-protect-right-vote-prosecute-election-fraud), [GovInfo January 6 collection](https://www.govinfo.gov/collection/january-6th-committee-final-report)
- EV011–EV012 and EV022: federal use-of-force reforms, de-escalation, intervention, medical-aid requirements, and later OIG-identified implementation gaps. [DOJ policy fact sheet](https://www.justice.gov/archives/olp/department-justice-fact-sheet-implementing-executive-order-advancing-effective-accountable), [DOJ OIG review](https://oig.justice.gov/news/doj-oig-releases-report-on-doj-law-enforcement-and-corrections-components-use-force-policies)
- EV013 and EV023: HRW criticism concerning migration, incarceration, policing, arms transfers, and human-rights conditionality. [HRW 2022 U.S. report](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2022/country-chapters/united-states)
- EV014 and EV026: ACLU criticism of biometric surveillance, privacy, AI governance, and EU–U.S. data-transfer safeguards. [ACLU civil-liberties review](https://www.aclu.org/news/capital-punishment/one-year-later-how-the-biden-administration-is-doing-on-civil-rights-and-civil-liberties), [ACLU data-transfer criticism](https://www.aclu.org/press-releases/new-biden-executive-order-on-eu-us-data-transfers-fails-adequately-protect-privacy)
- EV015–EV016: CHIPS program goals, $52.7 billion appropriations, implementation strategy, steering council, and congressional oversight questions. [NIST implementation strategy](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2022/09/biden-administration-releases-implementation-strategy-50-billion-chips), [CRS CHIPS report](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/R47523)
- EV017–EV018: IRA tax-credit implementation and $2.2 billion in RAISE infrastructure awards across all states. [Treasury IRA guidance](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy0923), [DOT RAISE awards](https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/bipartisan-infrastructure-law-raise-grants-2022-funding-projects-all-50-states)
- EV019: independent Brookings assessment of inflation, labor-market tightness, and policy constraints in 2022. [Brookings 2022 economic review](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/key-economic-policy-developments-in-2022-and-what-to-expect-in-2023/)
- EV020–EV021: CDC vaccination/global-response claims and GAO findings that only 39% of pandemic recommendations had been fully or partially addressed by March 2022. [CDC testimony](https://www.cdc.gov/washington/testimony/2022/t20220330.htm), [GAO pandemic review](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-22-105397)
- EV024: partisan House Republican allegations about Biden family business dealings; retained as adversarial context only, not an adjudicated finding. [House Oversight interim report](https://oversight.house.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/Interim-Staff-Report-A-President-Compromised-The-Biden-Family-Investigation-1.pdf)
- EV025: Biden financial disclosure and OGE compliance certification. [OGE filing](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Biden-Joseph-R.-2023-Annual-278.pdf)

### Chapter yield

- 1B: Strong formal evidence on arms control and nuclear-risk posture; weak on command safety, appointments, dual-use governance, and measurable end-state change.
- 2B: Strong on Ukraine assistance, diplomacy, and oversight; weak on Biden-specific civilian-harm responsibility, proxy control, public threat accuracy, and peace alternatives.
- 3B: Strong on federal policing safeguards; mixed/adverse evidence on migration, detention, surveillance, and implementation gaps. Local policing remains attribution-limited.
- 4B: Strong on voting-rights enforcement, institutional constraints, and oversight. Limited direct evidence of Biden manipulating elections, courts, media, or opposition.
- 5B: Strong on explicit CHIPS, IRA, and infrastructure programs and early implementation; mixed on inflation, distribution, and household effects; limited target-year durability evidence.
- 6B: Strong on vaccination and public-health administration; mixed on GAO-identified preparedness and oversight gaps; weak on group-level quality, affordability, political conditionality, and durability.
- 7B: Direct personal-nexus evidence remains thin. EV024 is a partisan allegation; EV025 is a formal disclosure/compliance record. Country corruption indicators were used only as context.
- 8B: Strong on program definition, legislation, coordination, and early implementation; mixed on COVID oversight and inflation; limited evidence on adaptation, outcomes, and durability across the full portfolio.

### Local structured audit

Retained as context or direct measurement where applicable:

- LF001–LF005: FAS nuclear inventory, 2014 inherited posture.
- LF050–LF101: UCDP conflict exposure and SIPRI military expenditure through 2022.
- LF197–LF253: CIRIGHTS, V-Dem, and PTS physical-integrity context.
- LF346–LF505: Freedom House, V-Dem, EIU, Polity, RSF, and WGI political-freedom context.
- LF577–LF719: GDP, consumption, inequality, capital formation, population, and longitudinal economic signals.
- LF764–LF771: HDI, life expectancy, schooling, immunization, and enrollment.
- LF816–LF819: corruption indicators.
- LF842–LF843: government effectiveness and regulatory quality.

These country-level facts were not personalized without narrative evidence. Missing local values were not treated as real-world zeros. LF448 was retained only as missing-value provenance.

### Reuse and source diversity

- Cross-chapter reuse was substantial for EV001–EV002, EV006–EV008, EV011–EV012, EV014, EV017–EV021, and EV023.
- EV006 and EV008 are same-report splits supporting distinct Ukraine-assistance and oversight claims.
- EV011 and EV022 are same-URL splits supporting distinct federal-policy and accountability claims.
- Source families represented: White House, Congress/CRS, State Department, DOJ, DOJ OIG, GovInfo, UN, NIST/Commerce, Treasury, DOT, CDC, GAO, Brookings, HRW, ACLU, House Oversight, and local structured datasets.
- Contrary evidence is preserved in EV012, EV013, EV014, EV019, EV021, EV023, EV024, and EV026.

### Rejected or limited material

Search-result snippets, Wikipedia, Reddit, current-period sources, unattributed opinion, and organization homepages were not retained. Official administration claims were used for formal acts and stated policy, not as sole proof of success or restraint. EV024 remains context-only because its conclusions are partisan and disputed.
